# lean-pkg page

render the README verification section from coverage.yaml, claims, the ledger and the receipts; stdout unless --write/--check/--out/--site/--html.

## Usage

```text
lean-pkg page [--write] [--check] [--out PATH] [--site DIR] [--html PATH] [--repo DIR]
              [--allow-private-manuscript] [--agent AGENT] [common flags] NAME
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

## Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `NAME` |   |
| `--write` | replace the marked block in the package README.md (append it when absent); prose outside the markers is untouched; not a registry write |
| `--check` | exit 1 when the README block is missing or stale, the lean-pkg credit is missing, or the Easley sentence has no backing Slurm receipt; with --site/--html also when those files are missing or stale; writes nothing |
| `--out PATH` | write the block here instead; README untouched |
| `--site DIR` | also write DIR/verification.md (the full page) and DIR/coverage.md (every row, its claims, inputs and notes) for MkDocs; with --check, compare them instead |
| `--html PATH` | also write one static HTML file (no script, no external asset) from the same data; with --check, compare it instead |
| `--repo DIR` | read the checkout DIR instead of the registered local_path, for this call only (never saved; for CI): DIR must be a git work tree, and when it has remotes one must be the package's repo; not with --write |
| `--allow-private-manuscript` | render against manuscript.version 'unposted'; the page then says so |
| `--agent AGENT` | with --write: the lease holder, when the package is leased |

## Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `page NAME` | render the README verification section (status capsule, paper-to-Lean map, Not formalized, trust boundary, reproduce, evidence, citation, license, acknowledgments) between `<!-- lean-pkg:page:begin -->` and `<!-- lean-pkg:page:end -->` from `coverage.yaml`, `claims.yaml`, the claims ledger (a row is *verified* only when the ledger closes it) and the receipts committed under `.lean-receipts/` (allow-listed fields only); deterministic; the public-safety scanner runs over the block and a blocking hit refuses; stdout by default; `--write` replaces only the marked block in the package `README.md` (appends it when absent), never commits and never writes the registry; `--check` exits 1 when the block is missing or stale, the lean-pkg credit is missing, or the README mentions the Easley Cluster without a backing Slurm receipt; `--out PATH` writes the block elsewhere; `--site DIR` also writes `DIR/verification.md` (the full page) and `DIR/coverage.md` (every row with its claims, declarations, ledger statuses, inputs and notes) for MkDocs, and `--html PATH` one static HTML file of both (no script, no external asset); with `--check` those files are compared instead (missing or stale: exit 1); user text is escaped in every output; `--repo DIR` reads that checkout instead of `local_path` for this call (CI; not with `--write`); `--json` gains `site_files[]` {path, status} and `repo_override` ([The verification page](../page.md)) | `[--write \| --check \| --out PATH]` `[--site DIR]` `[--html PATH]` `[--repo DIR]` `[--allow-private-manuscript]` `[--agent A]` |

## Exit codes

0 success (dry runs and no-ops included), 1 refused or failed, 2 usage error; see [Exit codes](../cli.md#exit-codes).

## JSON output

Top-level keys of `--json`, as recorded in the golden contract (tests/golden/json-keys.json):

- `page` (exit 0): `counts`, `current`, `easley`, `kind`, `ledger_digest`, `ledger_status`, `manuscript`, `markdown`, `name`, `ok`, `private_manuscript`, `problems`, `readme`, `receipts`, `repo_override`, `rows`, `site_files`, `unchanged`, `verified_rows`, `warnings`, `written`

## Examples

Print the README verification section rendered from coverage.yaml, the claims, the ledger and the receipts.

```bash
lean-pkg page my-proof
```

Replace the marked block in the package README.md (append it when absent).

```bash
lean-pkg page my-proof --write
```

Exit 1 when the README block is missing or stale; a CI step for the package.

```bash
lean-pkg page my-proof --check
```

Also write the docs pages and one self-contained HTML file.

```bash
lean-pkg page my-proof --site docs --html docs/verification.html
```
